svg.title: Potential energy between two light nuclei
svg.desc: Potential energy of two light nuclei versus their separation r. At large r the repulsive Coulomb force makes the energy positive and falling off slowly; closer in it rises to a hump, then plunges into a deep well where the attractive nuclear force takes over. A nucleus with enough energy to get over the hump is pulled together into the well; one without enough is repelled. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Coulomb repulsion converts approach kinetic energy into potential
Classical radial approach and return with U ∝ 1/r, stopping at U = E. The cursor sweeps separation,
not equal times. Fusion below a barrier additionally requires quantum tunneling.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
